## Purpose and Entry Points
PocketBase is a Go-embeddable, single-binary backend: SQLite persistence, REST-style APIs, auth, file storage, realtime subscriptions, and an embedded admin UI. Library construction begins at `pocketbase.go`; applications commonly instantiate it and call `Start()`. The standalone example is `examples/base/main.go`; CLI commands, including serving and superuser administration, are in `cmd/serve.go` and `cmd/superuser.go`.

## Application Lifecycle and Extension Boundary
`core/app.go` owns the application runtime and services. Its event system in `core/events.go` exposes lifecycle/request hooks used by Go applications and plugins; request context is modeled through `core/event_request.go`. The JavaScript extension runtime is a distinct plugin boundary: `plugins/jsvm/jsvm.go` and `plugins/jsvm/binds.go` host/bind application capabilities, while `plugins/jsvm/pool.go` manages VM execution resources.

## HTTP API, Routing, and Realtime
The serving layer registers API endpoints and middleware in `apis/serve.go` and `apis/middlewares.go`, on the custom router abstraction in `tools/router/router.go`. Domain endpoints split into record CRUD (`apis/record_crud.go`), authentication (`apis/record_auth.go`), and operational endpoints such as backup/settings. Realtime connections are handled in `apis/realtime.go` and backed by in-process subscription primitives in `tools/subscriptions/broker.go`; record/activity changes can therefore fan out to connected clients without an external message broker.

## Data Model, Persistence, and Querying
The core data boundary is dynamically defined collections, fields, and records: `core/collection_model.go`, `core/field.go`, and `core/record_model.go`. Collection definitions determine record-table synchronization (`core/collection_record_table_sync.go`) and validation (`core/collection_validate.go`). Database lifecycle, connections, and transactions reside in `core/db.go`, `core/db_connect.go`, and `core/db_tx.go`; the documented embedded engine is SQLite, with pure-Go/static-build support. Record querying/expansion is centralized in `core/record_query.go` and `core/record_query_expand.go`.

## Security and Identity Flows
Authentication supports password, OTP, OAuth2, refresh tokens, MFA, email verification/change, password reset, impersonation, and superusers. The public HTTP flow is implemented across `apis/record_auth_with_password.go`, `apis/record_auth_with_oauth2.go`, and `apis/record_auth_refresh.go`; persistent auth-related models include `core/external_auth_model.go`, `core/mfa_model.go`, and `core/otp_model.go`. JWT/cryptographic primitives are isolated in `tools/security/jwt.go` and `tools/security/crypto.go`; OAuth providers are adapters under `tools/auth/`.

## Files, Backups, Mail, and Operations
File fields connect record data to a pluggable filesystem boundary (`core/field_file.go`, `tools/filesystem/filesystem.go`). Storage supports local blobs and an S3-compatible implementation (`tools/filesystem/internal/s3blob/s3blob.go`), making object storage the principal external infrastructure option. Backup creation/restoration is core functionality in `core/backup_create.go` and `core/backup_restore.go`, exposed via `apis/backup.go`. Outbound mail is composed from record mail logic and templates (`mails/record.go`, `mails/templates/layout.go`) and sent through SMTP or sendmail adapters (`tools/mailer/smtp.go`, `tools/mailer/sendmail.go`).

## Admin UI and Schema Operations
The prebuilt admin dashboard is embedded by Go through `ui/embed.go`, with browser assets under `ui/dist/`; source UI routing begins at `ui/src/main.js`. It administers collections, records, logs, backups, storage, mail, cron, SQL, and settings. Schema/data evolution is versioned through `core/migrations_runner.go` and repository migrations in `migrations/`; the migration CLI/plugin layer is `plugins/migratecmd/migratecmd.go`.
